html:
Sambor Prei Kuk, in central Cambodia, was Ishanapura, capital of the kingdom of Chenla under King Isanavarman I in the early 7th century. Its brick temples are the oldest large group of temples in Cambodia.

Chenla took over from Funan and spread Khmer rule inland. The temples, many octagonal, honour Shiva and other Hindu gods, with carved lintels that set the style for later Khmer art.

Chenla later split into rival states, before Jayavarman II united them in 802. The site became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2017. See also Angkor Borei and Hinduism.
